original_question: If the quadratic polynomial P_c is nonrecurrent, does there exist a conformal metric of the form rho(z)|dz| with integrable singularities for which P_c is expanding on its Julia set?
target_in_paper: §1 (Local connectivity of Julia sets), Question 13: "If P_c is nonrecurrent does this imply the existence of a conformal metric (a metric of the form ρ(z)|dz| with integrable singularities) for which P_c is expanding on its Julia set?"
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's official wording. It correctly identifies the quadratic family P_c, the nonrecurrent hypothesis, the search for a conformal metric of the form ρ(z)|dz| with integrable singularities, and the conclusion that P_c should be expanding on its Julia set.
missing_details: The paper's notation is explicitly P_c(z)=z^2+c.

In this part of the paper, c is restricted to parameters for which the Julia set J(P_c) is connected; that scope is set immediately before the list of quadratic questions and remains in force for Question 13.
The problem list does not define 'nonrecurrent' here; to make the question stand-alone, one should specify that the unique critical point 0 of P_c is nonrecurrent under iteration.

The paper only parenthetically explains 'conformal metric' as a metric of the form ρ(z)|dz|; it does not further specify the domain of definition of ρ, so a stand-alone version should at least indicate that the metric is the one used to measure expansion on J(P_c).
The paper leaves 'expanding on its Julia set' implicit rather than formalizing the metric-expansion inequality, so the draft inherits that implicitness.
The nearby remark that Yoccoz had already proved local connectivity in the nonrecurrent case is context and motivation, not part of the hypothesis or conclusion.
The official target is a narrowly scoped quadratic-polynomial question only; it should not be broadened to general rational maps, all unicritical polynomials, or semihyperbolic maps in general.
refined_question: Let P_c(z)=z^2+c, with connected Julia set J(P_c). If the unique critical point 0 is nonrecurrent under iteration of P_c, must there exist a conformal metric of the form ρ(z)|dz|, allowing integrable singularities, with respect to which P_c is expanding on J(P_c)?
justification: In arXiv:math/9201271, the nearest official target is not a conjecture or theorem but §1, Question 13 of the problem list. Your draft is almost verbatim to that question. The only additions needed to make it stand-alone and paper-faithful are the explicit definition P_c(z)=z^2+c and the inherited scope that c ranges over parameters with connected Julia set. I kept the question strictly in the quadratic family and did not import stronger later reformulations (for example, requirements that the metric be Hölder/topologically equivalent to the Euclidean metric), because those are not part of the original 1990 problem-list statement.
